items.q: Two balls of different mass are dropped in a vacuum — which lands first?
items.correct: They land together: in a vacuum all objects fall with the same acceleration g.
items.misconception: The heavier ball lands first because gravity pulls on it harder.
items.random_wrong: The lighter ball lands first because it has less inertia.
items.why: The heavier ball has more weight, but also more mass, so a = F/m = g is the same for both. Only air resistance makes a feather fall slower in air.

items.q: A car travels at a steady 30 m/s along a straight, level road. What is the resultant force on it?
items.correct: Zero — at constant velocity the driving force and resistive forces are balanced.
items.misconception: A forward force, because it keeps moving forwards.
items.random_wrong: A backward force, because friction is winning.
items.why: Newton's first law: constant velocity means zero resultant force. A force is only needed to change velocity, not to maintain it.

items.q: An astronaut takes a 6 kg rock from Earth to the Moon. What changes?
items.correct: Its weight decreases (weaker gravity); its mass stays 6 kg.
items.misconception: Both its mass and its weight decrease.
items.random_wrong: Its mass decreases but its weight stays the same.
items.why: Mass is the amount of matter (kg) and is constant; weight is the gravitational force W = mg and depends on g, which is weaker on the Moon.
